The blade had a total of 172 film-cooling holes in 8 rows, with 3 of the rows having compound-angled shower-head holes.
The hole diameter was 0.381 mm, about 1% of the blade axial chord at mid-span.
The tip clearance region was about 1.3% of the blade span.
The final multi-block grid consisted of 2,205,760 cells, with 80 cells within each hole exit.
The y+ values were kept under 0.2 over the entire blade surface.
The heat transfer coefficient was highest in the leading edge region and in the tip region of the cooled, isothermal blade.
The film cooling effectiveness was lowest in the leading edge region and near the blade tip, especially over the suction surface.
The heat transfer coefficient was much higher on the shroud compared to the hub for both the cooled and uncooled cases.
The computed and given coolant mass flow rates matched very well, with the total coolant mass flow rate for the three staggered shower-head rows being the same as the given value.
The simulation required about 500 iterations to converge and took about 11s per iteration on the 16-processor NASA Ames supercomputer.
The k-ω turbulence model of Wilcox with Menter's modifications was used for modeling the turbulence.
Polynomial distributions of coolant velocity and temperature were specified at the hole exits.
The true oval shape of the hole exits was faithfully discretized using 80 control volumes per hole.
The multi-block grid was able to transition smoothly from a very fine structure near the hole boundaries to a coarse structure away from the holes.
The heat transfer coefficient on the cooled blade was generally lower than that on the uncooled blade, except in the shower-head region and the tip region on the suction side.
